documents.title: Gynecology Office Visit (outside)
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OB/GYN OFFICE NOTE
Date of service: 04/27/2020
Copy to primary care physician

Reason for visit: well-woman exam; contraception and STI prevention counseling.

23 y/o G0, graduate student, here for a routine gynecologic exam. She has recently begun a new relationship and wants to go over birth control and how to protect herself from infections, and asks whether she should be tested. No symptoms today. Cycles regular. LMP about two weeks ago. Denies any genital sores, abnormal discharge or burning with urination.

PMH: none. Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother - hypothyroidism; father - hypertension.
SH: never smoker; alcohol 1-2 drinks/week; graduate student.

Vitals: within normal limits.
Pelvic: external genitalia normal. Speculum: cervix without mucopurulent discharge. Bimanual normal; no cervical motion tenderness; no adnexal masses or tenderness.

Labs: RPR nonreactive. Gonorrhea/chlamydia NAAT negative.

Assessment/Plan:
1. Well-woman exam, normal.
2. Contraception counseling: reviewed combined pills, progestin-only options, the implant, copper and hormonal IUDs. She prefers to rely on condoms for now and will call if she wants to start a method.
3. STI prevention: syphilis screen negative, GC/CT negative. Encouraged consistent condom use with new partners.
Return as needed or in one year.

documents.title: Gynecology Office Visit (outside)
documents.author: gynecology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE OB/GYN OFFICE NOTE
Date of service: 07/29/2020
Sent in response to records request

CC: vaginal discharge.

Seen about three months after her well visit. For several months she has noticed a white discharge. No odor. No itching, burning or irritation. LMP began 14 days ago; cycles every 28 days. One partner; condoms not every time.

Meds: none. NKDA.

Vitals normal.
Speculum: small amount of white mucoid discharge at the cervical os. No erythema. No lesions. No sign of trauma.

Wet mount: numerous epithelial cells; rare PMNs; normal vaginal flora (lactobacilli predominant); no trichomonads; no clue cells. pH 4.5.

Impression: physiologic leukorrhea. No evidence of bacterial vaginosis, trichomoniasis or yeast.
Plan: reassured; no treatment needed. Reviewed what normal mid-cycle discharge looks like and when to come back (odor, itching, color change, pelvic pain).

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PHYSICAL (masked visit)

24 y/o grad student, classes remote this term. Feels well.

Interval: started seeing an outside gynecologist this spring. Had a well-woman visit in April (we have that note: syphilis screen and GC/CT negative, chose condoms for contraception). Went back in July for a white discharge she had noticed for a few months; she says they looked at it under the microscope and told her it was normal discharge, nothing to treat. No current symptoms. We never got the July note; requesting it.

No meds. NKDA. No tobacco. Light alcohol.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well. Heart and lungs normal. Abdomen soft. Pelvic deferred, followed by gyn.

A/P
1. Preventive: Pap next due 2021. Flu vaccine given.
2. Gyn care outside; records request sent for 7/29 visit.
3. Mood good, PHQ-2 of 1.

Year.

documents.body: Hi Leah, the gynecology note from July finally arrived. It matches what you told me: the discharge was normal, the microscope check showed no yeast, BV or trich, and no treatment was needed. Filed in your chart. Nothing for you to do.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PHYSICAL

Back on campus in person this fall, second year of her program. Feels well. No complaints. The discharge from last year is not bothering her; no itching or odor. Periods regular. Sexually active, not with one steady partner at the moment; condoms some of the time.

No meds. NKDA. Never smoker. 1-2 drinks a week. COVID series done in the spring.

Exam: vitals as charted. Healthy-appearing. Heart, lungs, abdomen normal. Pelvic: normal external genitalia; cervix appears normal; no discharge beyond scant clear secretions. Bimanual nontender.

A/P
1. Preventive: Pap (3 years since the first), GC/CT swab, CBC and fasting lipids for a baseline.
2. Physiologic leukorrhea, resolved; off the active list.
3. Talked about condoms with every new partner. She says she knows and is trying.
4. Flu shot today.

Next physical fall 2022.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record (outside)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT - PHYSICIAN DOCUMENTATION
Visit: 10/22/2021

Chief complaint: fever, malaise, rash x 2 weeks.

HPI: 25 y/o F. About two weeks of low energy, feeling feverish, and a rash that started on her chest and back and has spread down her arms and legs, now on her palms and the soles of her feet. Not itchy. When asked, she recalls a few painless sores in the genital area some months back that went away without treatment; she never had them checked. Last syphilis test she knows of was negative at a gyn visit about a year and a half ago. Several recent partners, condoms inconsistently.

PMH: none active. Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother hypothyroidism, father hypertension.

Exam: VS within normal limits. Diffuse nonpruritic maculopapular eruption over trunk and extremities including palms and soles. Generalized lymphadenopathy with palpable epitrochlear nodes bilaterally. Oropharynx clear. No meningismus. Neuro nonfocal; no visual complaints.

Results: RPR reactive, 1:64. TP-PA reactive. HIV Ag/Ab nonreactive.

ED course / MDM: presentation and serologies consistent with early (secondary) syphilis. No neurologic or ocular symptoms. Benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM given x1; observed 30 min, no reaction. Counseled on possible fever/myalgias in the first day after treatment. Health department partner services referral made. Abstain until rash resolved and partners treated.

Dx: Early syphilis, secondary.
Dispo: home. Follow up with PCP within 1-2 weeks; repeat RPR at 6 and 12 months.

documents.title: ER last night
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, I went to the ER last night for the rash I've had. They said it's syphilis and gave me a shot of penicillin in the hip. I feel kind of achy today but they warned me about that. They told me to see you in a week or two. Can I get an appointment? Kind of freaked out honestly.

documents.title: RE: ER last night
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for telling me, and I'm glad you went in. This is very treatable and the shot you got is the right treatment. The achiness the first day is expected; acetaminophen is fine. Our front desk will reach out Monday to book you for next week. If you get a headache that won't quit, vision changes, or anything that scares you, call the after-hours line.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Post-ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
FOLLOW-UP AFTER ED VISIT

Seen 10/22 at the regional ED (record received 10/27 and reviewed): two weeks of malaise and a rash on trunk, limbs, palms and soles; remote painless genital sores; RPR 1:64, TP-PA reactive, HIV negative. Treated with benzathine penicillin 2.4 MU IM once.

Since then: achy and warm for about a day after the shot, then better. Rash is fading and mostly gone from her hands. Energy coming back. Health department called her about partners; she gave them names.

Sexual history: several partners over the past year, condoms inconsistently. We talked about it plainly; she is not interested in a lecture and I did not give one.

Exam: vitals as charted, afebrile. A few faint coppery macules on forearms; palms and soles nearly clear. Small shotty nodes in the neck and groin. No mucosal lesions seen.

A/P
1. Early syphilis, treated. Repeat RPR at 6 months (late April) and 12 months (October with her physical). Expect a fourfold drop by 6-12 months. Avoid sex until rash gone and partners treated.
2. High-risk sexual behavior: multiple partners, inconsistent condoms. Condoms with each partner; regular testing here.
3. Old 'syphilis screening negative' entry from April 2020 closed out.

RPR order placed for April.
